instruction:
Schema: listings(id, city, price)
Rows where price is above the average
output: SELECT * FROM listings WHERE price > (SELECT AVG(price) FROM listings);

instruction:
Schema: listings(id, city, price)
Row with the highest price
output: SELECT * FROM listings WHERE price = (SELECT MAX(price) FROM listings);

instruction:
Schema: listings(id, city, price)
Row with the lowest price
output: SELECT * FROM listings WHERE price = (SELECT MIN(price) FROM listings);

instruction:
Schema: listings(id, city, price)
Rows where id is in a subquery from listings
output: SELECT * FROM listings WHERE id IN (SELECT DISTINCT id FROM listings);

instruction:
Schema: listings(id, city, price)
Rows where id is not in the set of values 1 and 2
output: SELECT * FROM listings WHERE id NOT IN (1, 2);

instruction:
Schema: listings(id, city, price)
Use EXISTS to find rows where a id appears more than once
output: SELECT * FROM listings t WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM listings t2 WHERE t2.id = t.id GROUP BY t2.id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1);

instruction:
Schema: listings(id, city, price)
Subquery in SELECT returning count per id
output: SELECT t.*, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM listings t2 WHERE t2.id = t.id) AS cnt FROM listings t;

instruction:
Schema: listings(id, city, price)
Rows where price > the maximum of city plus 100 in subquery
output: SELECT * FROM listings WHERE price > ((SELECT MAX(price) FROM listings) + 100);

instruction:
Schema: listings(id, city, price)
Second highest price using subquery
output: SELECT MAX(price) FROM listings WHERE price < (SELECT MAX(price) FROM listings);

instruction:
Schema: listings(id, city, price)
Correlated subquery: rows whose price is above the avg of their id
output: SELECT * FROM listings t WHERE price > (SELECT AVG(price) FROM listings t2 WHERE t2.id = t.id);

instruction:
Schema: listings(id, city, price)
Columns where price is greater than average in their group
output: SELECT * FROM listings t WHERE price >= (SELECT AVG(price) FROM listings t2 WHERE t2.id = t.id);

instruction:
Schema: listings(id, city, price)
Derived table returning count per id
output: SELECT sub.id, sub.cnt FROM (SELECT id, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM listings GROUP BY id) sub WHERE sub.cnt > 2;

instruction:
Schema: listings(id, city, price)
Subquery filtering rows with ANY operator
output: SELECT * FROM listings WHERE price = ANY (SELECT price FROM listings WHERE price < 50);

instruction:
Schema: listings(id, city, price)
Subquery filtering rows with ALL operator
output: SELECT * FROM listings WHERE price > ALL (SELECT AVG(price) FROM listings);

instruction:
Schema: listings(id, city, price)
Scalar subquery for a single value
output: SELECT (SELECT AVG(price) FROM listings) AS avg_val;

instruction:
Schema: listings(id, city, price)
Rows matching set from a subquery using IN
output: SELECT * FROM listings WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM listings GROUP BY id HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3);

instruction:
Schema: listings(id, city, price)
Largest value strictly less than the global maximum
output: SELECT price FROM listings ORDER BY price DESC LIMIT 1 OFFSET 1;

instruction:
Schema: listings(id, city, price)
Nested subquery: top values per group based on derived ranking
output: SELECT t.* FROM listings t WHERE t.price = (SELECT MAX(price) FROM listings t2 WHERE t2.id = t.id);

instruction:
Schema: listings(id, city, price)
Rows where city not present in a sub table
output: SELECT * FROM listings WHERE city NOT IN (SELECT city FROM listings WHERE price > 90);

instruction:
Schema: listings(id, city, price)
Subquery used to compare against the overall total
output: SELECT id, SUM(price) AS part FROM listings GROUP BY id HAVING SUM(price) > (SELECT AVG(price) FROM listings);

instruction:
Schema: listings(id, city, price)
Use a subquery to compute rolling reference count
output: SELECT t.id, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM listings t2 WHERE t2.id <= t.id) AS running FROM listings t;

instruction:
Schema: listings(id, city, price)
EXISTS correlated check to its own table values
output: SELECT * FROM listings t WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM listings t2 WHERE t2.id = t.id AND t2.price > t.price);

instruction:
Schema: listings(id, city, price)
Subquery comparing to the minimum plus a constant
output: SELECT * FROM listings WHERE price > (SELECT MIN(price) FROM listings) + 10;

instruction:
Schema: listings(id, city, price)
Subquery returning rows for a top slice group
output: SELECT * FROM listings WHERE price IN (SELECT price FROM listings ORDER BY price DESC LIMIT 5);

instruction:
Schema: listings(id, city, price)
Subquery joining a derived aggregate
output: SELECT t.* FROM listings t JOIN (SELECT id, MAX(price) mx FROM listings GROUP BY id) a ON a.id = t.id AND a.mx = t.price;
